Overview

Istanbul as a Business Centre

Istanbul is Türkiye's largest city and its commercial centre, with a population of about 15.75 million at the end of 2025 and an economy accounting for roughly 30 percent of national output. The city straddles the Bosphorus, the only passage between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean, which has made it a trading city for centuries. Its business districts in Levent, Maslak and Bomonti house bank, holding company and multinational regional headquarters, while the Istanbul-İzmit corridor is one of the country's main industrial regions. Two international airports, Istanbul Airport and Sabiha Gökçen, connect the city to Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia and Africa.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Istanbul because it is where Turkish family business groups are run, where exporters, contract manufacturers and trading companies are concentrated, and where many cross-border disputes involving Turkish parties are argued. Typical engagements include diligence on suppliers and acquisition targets, review of trading intermediaries whose flows touch the Black Sea, the Caucasus, Central Asia or the Middle East, tracing of assets held through Istanbul holding companies, and evidence gathering for arbitrations seated in the city. Construction and contracting groups based in Istanbul also work across the wider region, carrying their counterparty risk with them.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Istanbul

01

Supplier and contract manufacturer diligence

European and US buyers source textiles, automotive parts, furniture and food products through Istanbul-based manufacturers and agents. Diligence confirms who owns the supplier, whether production is subcontracted, how the business is financed and whether owners have litigation, insolvency or regulatory history.

02

Trading intermediaries and re-export risk

Istanbul trading companies often sit between European goods and buyers in the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Middle East. Engagements examine ownership, banking relationships, shipping patterns and counterparties to assess sanctions, export control and diversion exposure before onboarding or during a review.

03

Holding company ownership reconstruction

Turkish family groups commonly hold operating businesses through Istanbul holding companies with layered shareholdings. Work reconstructs control from Trade Registry Gazette announcements, court records and press coverage, noting where joint-stock share ledgers are not public and ownership cannot be fully documented.

04

Contracting group counterparty reviews

Istanbul-headquartered construction and engineering groups pursue projects across Africa, the Gulf and Central Asia. Joint venture partners and lenders review their project history, disputes, debt restructurings, political exposure and how subcontractors and agents have been used on earlier contracts.

05

Arbitration and enforcement support

Many disputes with Turkish parties are seated in Istanbul or must be enforced there. Investigative support identifies witnesses and documents for the hearing, then researches assets, affiliated companies and transfers that bear on enforcement through Istanbul courts.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Istanbul

Arbitration centres in Istanbul

The Istanbul Arbitration Centre (ISTAC), established in 2015 and described as the primary venue for arbitration within Türkiye, has separate national and international boards and offers fast-track, emergency arbitrator, mediation-arbitration and online hearing rules; it registered 263 cases in 2025. The Istanbul Chamber of Commerce runs ITOTAM, also founded in 2015. The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Arbitration Centre is headquartered in Istanbul and issued new rules in January 2026.

Istanbul courts and arbitration

Istanbul has the largest concentration of commercial courts in Türkiye and its own regional court of appeal. Under International Arbitration Law No. 4686 of 2001, set-aside applications against international awards must be filed within 30 days and, since 2018, go directly to the regional courts of appeal. Recent decisions of the Istanbul Regional Court of Appeal on set-aside and enforcement are closely followed by practitioners.

Trade registry and chamber

Companies seated in Istanbul are registered with the trade registry directorate operating within the Istanbul Chamber of Commerce, one of the largest chambers in the region. Registered matters such as incorporation, capital changes and director appointments are announced in the Turkish Trade Registry Gazette, which is the usual starting point for reconstructing an Istanbul company's history. Gazette entries are dated, which helps build a timeline.

Financial market institutions

Borsa Istanbul, the country's exchange, operates in the city, and the Istanbul Financial Center in the Finanskent quarter near Ataşehir on the Asian side houses the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency, the Capital Markets Board and national banks. Disclosures by listed Istanbul companies are a useful source for related-party transactions, major shareholders and litigation, though most Istanbul businesses are privately held and disclose far less. Media coverage and court records, reviewed in Turkish, usually fill the gap.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Istanbul

For Istanbul matters TDSC begins by mapping which entities are registered in the city and which sit elsewhere in Türkiye or offshore, and by screening every counterparty and transaction flow for sanctions and export control exposure before research starts. Work draws on Trade Registry Gazette announcements, court information available through lawful means, exchange disclosures and Turkish-language media, reviewed by Turkish speakers. Where interviews, document retrieval or court filings in Istanbul are needed, TDSC coordinates qualified local professionals and works under the direction of the client's Turkish counsel, given that Türkiye has no licensing regime for private investigators that we have identified and that personal data collection is tightly constrained. Reports separate documented facts from inference.

TDSC has no office in Istanbul. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Istanbul: Frequently Asked Questions

Why is Istanbul central to most Turkish matters?

Istanbul produces about 30 percent of Türkiye's GDP and hosts most holding companies, banks, exporters and the leading law firms. Even when factories or projects are in Anatolia or abroad, ownership, finance and decision-making usually run through Istanbul, so records, witnesses and assets relevant to an investigation are often found there.

Which arbitration institutions are based in Istanbul?

The Istanbul Arbitration Centre (ISTAC), established in 2015, is the most active, with 263 cases filed in 2025. The Istanbul Chamber of Commerce runs ITOTAM, and the OIC Arbitration Centre is also headquartered in the city. ICC and other international arbitrations are frequently seated in Istanbul as well.

How can we learn the history of an Istanbul company?

Registered events such as incorporation, capital changes, address changes and director appointments are announced in the Turkish Trade Registry Gazette, and the company file is held by the trade registry within the Istanbul Chamber of Commerce. Shareholders of joint-stock companies are generally not public, so ownership often has to be pieced together from several sources.

Does trade through Istanbul raise sanctions concerns?

It can. Istanbul's role as a hub for trade with the Black Sea region, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Middle East means some intermediaries handle goods destined for restricted end users. Diligence on ownership, shipping routes and banking relationships helps identify that exposure before a transaction proceeds.

Does TDSC have an office in Istanbul?

No. TDSC is based in Nashville, Tennessee and has no office or staff in Türkiye. Engagements touching Istanbul are scoped and managed from Nashville, and where local work is required TDSC coordinates qualified Turkish professionals and works with the client's Turkish counsel. Field work is never presented as TDSC's own.
